defect_class: A test asserting that something is absent, refused or not found is fed inputs under which it could never be present or allowed, so it passes whether or not the code under test works.
why_picked: 1. Defect class: a test of an absence (not found, refused, filtered out) is fed inputs that can never produce the thing, so it is green with the rule under test removed. 2. No current rule covers it: engineering-principles.md's Testing principles carry "A test of a choice is fed inputs that separate the alternatives" (quoted as `before`), which governs which of several rules applies, not whether an absence is reachable at all; implementer-brief.md, implement.md and sdd-dispatch.md say nothing on negative assertions. 3. It generalises: the same run raised it twice in independent files of one round — F27, a by-id route matrix whose child path variables were random ids, so every route answered 404 whether or not the ownership check ran, and F26, a week test asserting an owner absent while no input gave that owner any workout — and the shape recurs in every authorization, visibility-filter, deletion and not-found test in any language or layer. 4. It is a principle, not a patch: "an absence is asserted beside a positive control" names no route, id scheme or framework; it is the negative-assertion counterpart of the existing choice rule.
before:
**A test of a choice is fed inputs that separate the alternatives.** When a test pins which
rule the code applies (an order, a precedence, a grouping, which of two sources wins), its
inputs make every plausible alternative rule produce a different result. Inputs on which the
alternatives agree leave the choice unpinned and the test green against its mutants: the
busiest item also first by name, a single group where the rule groups, two sources holding
one value.
after:
**A test of a choice is fed inputs that separate the alternatives.** When a test pins which
rule the code applies (an order, a precedence, a grouping, which of two sources wins), its
inputs make every plausible alternative rule produce a different result. Inputs on which the
alternatives agree leave the choice unpinned and the test green against its mutants: the
busiest item also first by name, a single group where the rule groups, two sources holding
one value.

**A test of an absence carries its positive control.** When a test asserts that something is
absent, refused or not found — a row filtered out, a request answered 404 or 403, an item missing
from a list — its inputs make that thing present or allowed once the rule under test is taken
away: ids that resolve to real rows, the excluded item holding data that would otherwise show.
The test asserts that control beside the absence — the same call under the rightful owner finds
the row, the unfiltered read lists the item — so inputs that could never produce the thing fail
the control instead of passing the absence.
